items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Your diamond ring could resell for half what you paid. A lab diamond costs up to ninety percent less. So what did you pay for?
Narrator
De Beers once controlled most of the world's diamonds.
Narrator
In nineteen forty-seven, their ad agency wrote four words: A Diamond Is Forever.
Narrator
So why does forever matter so much?
Narrator
Because forever means never resell. If nobody sells, nobody finds out what it's really worth.
Narrator
Romantic. And very good for business.
Narrator
And that's not even the cleverest part.
Narrator
Later ads asked how to make two months' salary last forever. Brides with diamond rings went from ten percent to about eighty percent.
Narrator
Now labs grow the same stone, and De Beers' owner has written it down by six point eight billion dollars.
Narrator
The rarity was never in the stone. It was in the story.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich, self-satisfied] Amateurs. I'm actually rare.
Narrator
Comment: mined or lab-grown, which would you buy?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
